newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma arrests 28 NLD members after student protest.
newsitem.headline: Burma arrests 28 NLD members after student protest.

text.p: A leader of Burma's opposition National League for Democracy (NLD) said on Thursday the government had arrested 28 of its members in the past five days for alleged connections to a student street protest last week.

NLD deputy leader U Tin Oo said the arrested members included 13 from the NLD's youth wing and one party politician who won a general election in 1990 that was not recognised by the ruling military government.
Tin Oo said the NLD MP was detained for nearly one day before his release on Wednesday.
Government spokesmen were not immediately available for comment.
The NLD said earlier it was not connected with student protests in the past week but a government spokesman charged on Monday that some NLD members had instigated the demonstrations.

Tin Oo told Reuters the arrested NLD members were onlookers during the protest by over 500 students of the Yangon University at a busy road junction and they did not take part in the demonstration which was dispersed by force early on Saturday.

He said six of those arrested had been released after interrogation. "They were warned before their release not to talk about their arrest and questioning or they would be violating the Government Secrets Act," Tin Oo said.

The NLD leader said government intelligence officers mostly picked up the NLD members near the house of opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi after their faces matched those in pictures taken by government agents near the scene of the Friday protest.

The government had said soldiers and police briefly detained 264 students and sympathisers taking part in the protest which, along with another demonstration on December 2, was among the biggest seen in Rangoon since the 1988 pro-democracy uprisings.
Tin Oo said NLD members still being detained had been sent to the maximum security Insein prison to await trials.
The NLD leader said a laundry worker not associated with the party died during the scuffles at the junction.
"The man was brutally beaten and taken to hospital. His family was told only days later after his funeral," Tin Oo said.
